newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan army chief gives gangs ultimatum.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan army chief gives gangs ultimatum.

text.p: Nicaragua's army chief said on Tuesday that peace talks between the government and armed gangs left over from the 1980s civil war were the gangs' last chance to disarm or face military action.

Army chief Gen. Joaquin Cuadra told reporters talks had begun between the government team headed by Defence Minister Jaime Cuadra and the gangs, vestiges of combatants from both sides in the civil war. The parties have assembled in neutral "peace zones" to negotiate the terms of the gangs' disarmament.

"We are going to put a final point to it here. We have opened a door, we hope these people respond to President Arnoldo Aleman's peace initiative, and if in the time established they have not agreed we will have to move on to other measures," Cuadra said. "The army is always ready to fulfil its function."
Aleman has said he wants the problem of the gangs resolved by the end of February or he will bring the weight of the law on the gangs, but he has not set an actual deadline date.

Nicaragua's civil war ended in 1990, but many former combatants later re-armed to protest what they see as the government's failure to fulfil the terms of the peace treaty. The gangs are known for robbing and kidnapping farmers in the countryside.

The army estimates that 500 members of 33 armed bands loosely linked to the former Contra rebels or left-wing Sandinista army continued to operate in remote regions of the north and central provinces of Jinotega, Matagalpa and Chontales.

Despite repeated government amnesties and offers to help the gangs return to civilian life, the problem has not gone away. Since 1990, armed bands have killed 1,000 people, wounded 400 and kidnapped 600 civilians, according to army figures.

Cuadra said Nicaragua's violent countryside cannot be pacified by military means alone, but needs programmes that deal with the rural poverty and unemployment that is the breeding ground for this violence.
